title: Individual local face differentials admit inner inverses
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $r\in\mathbb N$, $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$, $G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$. Let $C$ be the restriction to $U_i$ of the integer extension by zero of the alternating Čech sheaf complex [def-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-construction]. For each integer $k$ there exists a morphism $s:C^{k+1}\to C^k$ such that $d_k s d_k=d_k$. There is no asserted relation between the choices for adjacent degrees and no assertion of exactness.

source.place: Tag 02FU (cohomology-lemma-covering-resolution), Signed insertion applied only to boundaries in the local insertion computation; increasing tuples as in Tag 01FM

proof.text: Use the presheaf positive insertion identity to obtain s:P(p+1)→K(Pp) and t:P(p+2)→K(P(p+1)) with restriction ν=s K(d)+d t. Put T=module sheafification followed by restriction to U i. By the cap-unit local isomorphism theorem, T(ν) is invertible on both relevant terms. Set s'=T(s) T(ν_p)^{-1} and t'=T(t) T(ν_(p+1))^{-1}. Naturality gives T(d_p) T(ν_(p+1))=T(ν_p) T(K(d_p)). Postcompose s' T(d_p)+T(d_(p+1)) t' with T(ν_(p+1)); cancel the inverse units and use additivity to identify the result with T(ν_(p+1)). Cancelling this isomorphism yields the identity in natural degree p+1. The private lemma alternatingCechSheaf_restrict_natural_insertion proves this step in Lean.

For k≥0 put p=k.toNat. Precompose s' d_p+d_(p+1) t'=id by d_p. The complex equation d_p d_(p+1)=0 yields d_p s' d_p=d_p. Apply the functor to extendXIso at k and k+1. Mathlib extend_d_eq writes the integer differential as e_k d_p e_(k+1)^{-1}. Conjugate s' as e_(k+1) s' e_k^{-1}. Cancellation of the inverse isomorphisms in the triple composite proves the required integer equation.

If k<0, no natural number maps to k under embeddingUpNat. Mathlib isZero_extend_X makes the source term zero, and map_isZero preserves this under open restriction. Choose the zero morphism s; all morphisms out of this zero source agree, so d s d=d. This includes k=-1, regardless of the degree-zero target.

lean.statement:
theorem alternatingCechSheaf_restrict_differential_inner_inverse
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {r : ℕ} (U : Fin r → X.Opens) (G : X.Modules) (i : Fin r)
    (k : ℤ) :
    let F := Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι
    let C := (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
      ((alternatingCechSheafComplex U G).extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)
    ∃ s : C.X (k + 1) ⟶ C.X k,
      C.d k (k + 1) ≫ s ≫ C.d k (k + 1) = C.d k (k + 1)
